summary: Production behaviour is correct and in scope. No new object-store request is added: the only new read on the commit path is CommitLog.epoch(), an in-memory field, and the checkpoint/delta PUT rates are unchanged -- request rate still scales with deltas and AZs, never with pods, records or indices. Both layouts are selected, never mutated: a delta with no Attribution still encodes v0/kind-0 and a checkpoint with no pointer still encodes VERSION 0, so both legacy goldens hold. The pointer records the applied sequence passed in by the caller rather than log.nextSequence(), the merge is max-within-incarnation and replaces across one (both halves of the PodState move together, so the watermark and the pointer can never disagree), decode bounds both attribution lengths before the int cast in both formats, PodState refuses a half-pointer and an incarnation without one, and the presence flag is enumerated. The minting site is right: incarnationId is a final field of DefaultIngest, one per instance, and DefaultIngest is the only construction site of CommitRequest in main. Three findings, all comment-truth in production files, none behavioural.

findings.finding: The encode() contract javadoc still describes only two layouts and is now false for every production delta. It says "ENCODING IS CANONICAL AND VERSION-SELECTING (ADR-0032): one segment emits v0, byte-for-byte what every delta written before M4.7 says; two or more emit v1 kinded, kind 0" and then "SO A SINGLE-SEGMENT v1 DELTA DECODES BUT IS NEVER WRITTEN, and that asymmetry is bought deliberately". Since CommitLog.commitAll now attaches an Attribution to every submission, EVERY delta a live sequencer writes takes the new branch at line 145 and emits v1-kinded, kind 3 -- including the single-segment case. KIND_DELTA_ATTRIBUTED is not named anywhere in this javadoc; only the inline comment inside the method body mentions it.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader of the published contract on the format's only public encoder concludes that a single-segment delta in a bucket is v0 bytes and that a single-segment v1-kinded delta is never written. Acting on it: a recovery or forensic tool treats a single-segment kind-3 object -- the shape of every production commit after this lands -- as a shape that cannot exist, or a later format change re-uses the 'one segment implies v0' rule and writes an attributed single-flush commit as v0, silently dropping the pod attribution the checkpoint's window is rebuilt from. The javadoc's own 'round-trip stability is defined over CANONICAL encodings' sentence then names a canonical set that excludes the canonical encoding.
findings.recommendation: State the three-way selection in the javadoc (attribution -> kind 3 regardless of segment count; else one segment -> v0; else kind 0), or delete the two paragraphs rather than rewrite them -- review.md rule two-round-cap's tail: the prose that keeps being wrong is cheaper deleted.

findings.finding: The rationale for the enumerated version guard is false as written, and the commit's own test says so. The comment reads "AN ENUMERATED SET, never `version <= VERSION_ATTRIBUTED`: a range would decode a future v2 body with v1's layout, which is the guess CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest exists to forbid." With VERSION_ATTRIBUTED == 1, `version <= VERSION_ATTRIBUTED` refuses 2, so the stated consequence does not follow; and if the bound were later raised, decodeBody branches only on `version == VERSION_ATTRIBUTED`, so an admitted unknown version would be decoded with the v0 layout, not v1's. CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest.java:129-135, edited in this same commit, states the correct discriminator: "`bytes[7] = 9` is refused by an enumerated set AND by `version <= VERSION_ATTRIBUTED` alike ... A negative int passes a `<=` comparison and fails an enumeration, which is the only shape that tells them apart". The test comment was corrected and the production comment it duplicates was not.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever adds VERSION 2 reads this comment, believes the enumeration already guards against a future body being misparsed, and relaxes the guard to a range while adding only the new writer branch. decodeBody's else-arm then parses a v2 body with the v0 layout: no presence flag is consumed, so every pod slot decodes as bare, every incarnation and pointer is silently dropped, and the idempotency window comes back empty from a checkpoint that is not corrupt -- the exact silent-window failure ADR-0036's enumerated-set clause exists to prevent, reached because the comment named the wrong mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Replace the reason with the measured one already written in CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest -- only a NEGATIVE version separates the two forms -- or delete the reason and keep the code.

findings.finding: The replacement class javadoc overstates what landed. "THE PER-POD SLOT IS NO LONGER PROCESS-LOCAL" is contradicted eleven lines later by "WHAT REMAINS PROCESS-LOCAL is the in-memory map below"; "a successor rebuilds the window from the uncheckpointed TAIL" and "a replay older than the newest checkpoint is answerable at all" are both present tense for code that does not exist -- verified: no file under any src/main reads Checkpoint.pods(), ChainReplay consumes only streams() and sequence(), and nothing reads SegmentCommit.attribution(). This commit's own test theFirstCheckpointAfterATakeoverCarriesNoPodsAtAll (CheckpointWriterContentTest.java:205) still asserts the opposite and still holds. The deleted paragraph pointed at that test; the replacement does not, so the hole is now described as closed and its pin is unreferenced.
findings.failure_scenario: An M4.10d session opens the file it must change, reads that the successor already rebuilds the window from the tail and that a pre-checkpoint replay is already answerable, and implements only the refusal rule. Nothing folds the tail's Attribution into CheckpointWriter.pods, so after every takeover the window is empty exactly when duplicates are likeliest, and a replayed flush is assigned a second offset range -- the harm ADR-0036 exists to bound. The M4.10d backlog row does state the fold is its job, which is the only thing keeping this at minor.
findings.recommendation: Make the tense conditional ("the chain now CARRIES what a successor needs; nothing reads it yet -- M4.10d owns the fold") and re-name theFirstCheckpointAfterATakeoverCarriesNoPodsAtAll as the pin that still holds.

not_findings: Cost: no get/put/list/stat is added or moved. capture()'s new pointerEpoch is CommitLog.epoch(), a field read; observe()'s extra argument is delta.sequence(). Checkpoint PUT rate is still one per K deltas or per tick, delta PUT rate still one per commitAll. Object size grows by podId+incarnationId per segment and ~40 bytes per pod slot, which is bytes, not requests.

Rollout: every delta and every checkpoint written after this lands is a shape an older binary refuses (unknown kind 3, unsupported version 1), so a failover to a not-yet-upgraded leader would surface as 'store unreachable'. Not raised as a finding: no release exists, no consumer or plugin module decodes ChainEntry (verified by grep across src/main), and non-negotiable 8 requires reader and writer in one commit.

readSegment's segment-key length is still unbounded before its int cast, unlike the two attribution lengths beside it. Pre-existing, not introduced here; it wants a backlog row, not a change in this commit.
